senses.definition: The one most likely to win right now, while the outcome is still open.
senses.caution: Naming one changes the race. In a vendor evaluation, putting it in writing before scoring closes makes the process look decided, and that is precisely the sentence that resurfaces in a procurement challenge - keep it to conversation. It also paints a target on whoever you name, and if they lose, the room remembers that you called it early.
senses.example: Off the record the Swiss vendor is the frontrunner, but nothing goes in writing until scoring closes.

cues.text: Two candidates are left for a director role and one is clearly ahead. You are saying so to a peer over coffee, not putting it in an email.
A sponsor asks which supplier is likely to win while the scoring is still open, and you want a word that reports a position without announcing a decision.
Friends are arguing about who takes over as captain next season, and one name is obviously ahead of the others.
You and your partner have seen six flats and one is well ahead of the rest, though nothing is decided and you may still see more.

distractors: The one you actually use every day, as opposed to the one kept for special cases.
A funded team that concentrates a scarce skill in one place and sets how it is used.
Weight and seriousness in how a person carries themselves.
A rule of thumb that usually works.
The most senior people in an organisation.
